newsitem.title: CANADA: Cargill stops slaughter at strike-hit Alberta plan.
newsitem.headline: Cargill stops slaughter at strike-hit Alberta plan.

text.p: Cargill Ltd stopped slaughtering cattle at its strike-hit High River, Alberta meat-packing plant and was processing meat products from inventory, a Cargill executive said on Friday.
But the supply was expected to last just a few more days, Cargill vice-president Barb Eisman said in a telephone interview.
"That work is being done by supervisory personnel," Eisman said.
About 1,500 workers at the company's Cargill Foods Ltd plant walked off the job in a strike that began on Thursday.
Workers at the plant in High River, Alberta, 30 km south of Calgary, set up picket lines after talks broke off between the company and the United Food and Commercial Workers union late on Wednesday.
The plant processes about 4,000 head of cattle a day, making it one of Canada's largest.
Eisman said company and UCFW bargaining officials had not resumed talks since the picket lines went up.
"There was a contract offer made at 1 p.m. yesterday. That contract is going to be voted on by the union on Sunday afternoon," she said.
Eisman declined to comment on reports that the offer to the employees was a final one.
She also would not say whether Cargill would hire replacement workers should the strike continue after Sunday.
Cargill Ltd is a unit of Minneapolis-based Cargill Inc, the world's largest grain trader and one of the leading meatpackers in the United States.
